summary: Congonhas–Deputado Freitas Nobre Airport (CGH) is one of Brazil's busiest airports, located in the Jabaquara district just 8 km south of central São Paulo. It primarily serves domestic flights and is renowned for its remarkably short runway set amid the dense urban landscape. The airport's proximity to the city center and dramatic landing approach make it one of the most distinctive urban airports in the world.
faqs:
Q: Does Congonhas Airport handle international flights?
A: No, Congonhas (CGH) is a domestic-only airport. International travelers should use São Paulo–Guarulhos International Airport (GRU) instead.

Q: How far is Congonhas from São Paulo city center?
A: The airport is approximately 8 km (5 miles) from downtown São Paulo, making it one of the closest major airports to any major city center in the world.

Q: Why is Congonhas's runway considered challenging?
A: The short runway requires precise approach procedures, and the airport is surrounded by dense urban development, which has historically raised safety considerations. Strict pilot qualifications are required for landing there.

Q: Is there public transit access to the airport?
A: Yes, Congonhas Station on São Paulo's Line 5 (Lilac) metro provides direct access to the terminal building.
